reason: jsdom 30.0.0 only raises the supported Node.js range to ^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0 (engines field), with no API change.

Sent httpVersion: 2 requests with an explicit proxy through a local HTTP/1 proxy to a local h2c server on 1.16.1 and 1.20.0: both fail (1.16.1 sends HTTP/2 frames to the proxy and rejects with ERR_HTTP2_ERROR, 1.20.0 rejects with ERR_NOT_SUPPORT), so no working code for the old version depended on it and only the error code differs.

On jsdom 29.1.1 window.close() empties the document (getElementById returns null, serialize() throws), so code written for it reads or serializes the DOM before closing, which still works on 30.1.3; tried a render-then-close helper and found no plausible code that depends on the document being torn down.

jest-runtime 30.5.2 gates the new order on vm.SourceTextModule.prototype.hasAsyncGraph (Node 24.9+), which is undefined on the Node 22.22.3 the benchmark runs, so only the old linking-time order can be exercised.

In the pinned 5.104.5, usePrefetchQuery still fetches when enabled is false (queryClient.query() ignores enabled), and skipToken and select give the same cache outcome as 5.100.14 (checked by rendering the hook and calling both clients), so the pinned version does not behave as the entry says.

Sent requests through a local proxy with NO_PROXY set to CIDR, exact-IP and hostname lists on 1.16.1 and 1.20.0: only CIDR entries differ (ignored on 1.16.1, so requests went through the proxy; matched on 1.20.0), so code written for 1.16 could not use them and none plausibly depends on a CIDR entry being ignored.

observeTimeline was an undocumented internal export shared between framer-motion and motion-dom (the changelog calls it internal and restored it in 13.5.1 only for mixed internal package versions); app code tracks scroll progress with the documented scroll()/useScroll, which are unchanged, and no plausible app code imports it.

In lucide-react 1.59.0 Angry, Annoyed, Laugh, Meh, Frown, Smile and SmilePlus are plain alias exports of the new Face* icons with no @deprecated tag (TypeScript 6 reports no 6385/6387 suggestion, while the SwissFranc control is reported) and rendering them emits no warning.

In lucide-react 1.59.0 History (and HistoryIcon, LucideHistory) is a plain alias export of RotateCcwClock with no @deprecated tag (TypeScript 6 reports no 6385/6387 suggestion) and rendering it emits no warning; the deprecation is only in Lucides icon metadata, which lucide-react doesnt ship.

In lucide-react 1.59.0 Album, BookMarked and Building2 are plain alias exports of SquareBookmark, BookBookmark and BuildingComplex with no @deprecated tag (TypeScript 6 reports no 6385/6387 suggestion, while the SwissFranc control is reported) and rendering them emits no warning.

Ran a jest test on 30.4.2 and 30.5.2: process.getBuiltinModule("node:process") used to return the host process (env set in the test invisible) and "node:module" the unhooked module, and now returns the sandbox ones; code written for 30.4 reads the global process and require, which behave the same on both, and the only code that could depend on getting the host objects (bypassing the sandbox or jest mocks) is not plausible application code.

MotionPath is the protocol between a path factory and motion's animation engine, and the only documented use, passing arc() as transition.path, is unchanged; implementing or calling animateVisualElement means driving undocumented VisualElement internals (tried a custom wrapper around arc(), which TypeScript 6 does flag with 6387), so no plausible application code depends on it.
RTK 2.13.0 only raises its supported TypeScript range to 5.6+ (the release notes say the exports and APIs are unchanged from 2.12), with no API change.
